title: Maximum parsimony as a named fewest-changes criterion
dek: Wikipedia parsimony: minimise substitutions on a tree. Not a likelihood, and inconsistent on some long-branch patterns.
story: Maximum parsimony on Wikipedia is a criterion: choose the tree (and a mapping of changes) that needs the fewest substitutions. Fitch/Sankoff algorithms compute the score. It is philosophy-adjacent ('simplest history') and statistically fragile.
Felsenstein long-branch attraction is the celebrity inconsistency: parsimony can prefer the wrong tree with more data. Likelihood with a decent Q is the usual repair (stats-trees).
In TB, homoplasy from selection or recombination looks like extra changes. Parsimony will still return a number.
deep: Unweighted parsimony treats every change as equal; reality does not.
Dolce/Dollo variants are special-case costs, still not likelihoods.
Consistency results exist on some models; do not quote them as a blanket guarantee.
Do not report parsimony scores as log-likelihoods.

visual.caption: Parsimony minimises a count. Likelihood maximises P(data|tree,Q). Same trees as candidates, different objective.
